entries.claim: Before leading Television, Tom Verlaine embraced the jazz of John Coltrane and Albert Ayler as a teenage saxophonist.

sources.title: Bernard Gendron: Between Montmartre and the Mudd Club (University of Chicago Press)
sources.evidence: Academic book excerpt, Television section: Verlaine heard Coltrane, took up saxophone, and became an Ayler devotee.

sources.title: Patti Smith: He Was Tom Verlaine (The New Yorker)
sources.evidence: Personal remembrance: Verlaine played saxophone in high school and embraced Coltrane and Ayler.

entries.claim: Metallica recorded Black Sabbath’s “Sabbra Cadabra”, inserting a passage from “A National Acrobat”.

sources.title: Metallica: Sabbra Cadabra — official song credits
sources.evidence: Official credits identify Black Sabbath and the excerpt of A National Acrobat.

sources.title: Metal Hammer: The story of Metallica’s Garage Inc.
sources.evidence: Track 3 discussion identifies the Sabbath cover and the inserted passage; includes contemporary band comments.

entries.claim: Oasis included their cover of the Beatles’ “I Am the Walrus” on The Masterplan.

sources.title: Apple Music: The Masterplan — editorial album notes
sources.evidence: Editorial album notes identify I Am the Walrus as a Beatles cover.

sources.title: Pitchfork: Oasis — The Masterplan
sources.evidence: Independent album review discusses the live Beatles cover on the compilation.

entries.claim: The Beatles recorded “Twist and Shout” after the Isley Brothers made it an R&B hit.

sources.title: Charles Gower Price: Sources of American Styles in the Music of the Beatles (American Music, 1997)
sources.evidence: Peer-reviewed article, pp. 208–209 and 225: identifies the Isley model and compares the recordings.

sources.title: Associated Press: Rudolph Isley, founding member of Isley Brothers, dies at 84
sources.evidence: Reports the R&B hit and its subsequent inclusion on the Beatles debut.

entries.claim: The Rolling Stones released the blues song “Little Red Rooster” as a single.

sources.title: John Covach: The Rolling Stones — Albums and Singles, 1963–1974 (Cambridge University Press)
sources.evidence: Academic chapter, pp. 7–8, documents the Howlin’ Wolf song and the Stones blues single.

sources.title: Matthew Greenwald: Little Red Rooster (AllMusic)
sources.evidence: Editorial song review explicitly calls the Stones single a straight blues song.

entries.claim: Led Zeppelin reworked “When the Levee Breaks”, originally recorded by Kansas Joe McCoy and Memphis Minnie.

sources.title: Charles Shaar Murray: Led Zeppelin, Memphis Minnie, and the levee that broke (Classic Rock)
sources.evidence: Traces the 1929 recording by McCoy and Minnie to the Zeppelin adaptation; distinguishes McCoy’s writing and singing from Minnie’s guitar.

sources.title: Trevor de Clercq: Measuring a Measure (Music Theory Online 22.3)
sources.evidence: Peer-reviewed analysis, section 4.2–4.5, compares the original blues recording with Zeppelin’s 1971 version.

entries.claim: Before adopting the name Black Sabbath, the band played blues under the name Earth.

sources.title: Rolling Stone: Heavy Metal, Year One — The Inside Story of Black Sabbath’s Groundbreaking Debut
sources.evidence: Oral history documents Earth’s electric-blues repertoire with musicians and manager as witnesses.

sources.title: Guitar World: Original Members of Black Sabbath Look Back on 30-Plus Years of Demonic Riffing
sources.evidence: Separate 2001 interview: Geezer Butler describes Earth as a straight blues band.

entries.claim: Elvis Presley recorded “Hound Dog”, the song first recorded by Big Mama Thornton.

sources.title: Smithsonian Folkways: Big Mama Thornton
sources.evidence: Identifies Thornton’s first release and Presley’s later recording.

sources.title: Michael Sporke: Hound Dog — Big Mama Thornton (Library of Congress)
sources.evidence: National Recording Registry essay describes Thornton’s original and Presley’s later version; no claim that Presley copied her arrangement.

entries.claim: Bob Dylan recorded Blind Lemon Jefferson’s “See That My Grave Is Kept Clean” for his debut album.

sources.title: Bob Dylan: The Basement Tapes Complete — official liner notes
sources.evidence: Notes for One Kind Favor identify the alternate title, Jefferson association, and Dylan’s debut recording.

sources.title: Oxford University Press: Bob Dylan — A first listen
sources.evidence: Meghann Wilhoite’s first-album review lists the song and credits Blind Lemon Jefferson.

entries.claim: The Clash recorded a cover of Junior Murvin’s reggae song “Police and Thieves”.

sources.title: The Clash: The Clash — official album notes
sources.evidence: Official debut album page identifies the Murvin cover and reggae connection.

sources.title: Pitchfork: R.I.P. Reggae Singer Junior Murvin
sources.evidence: Identifies Murvin’s reggae hit and subsequent Clash cover.

entries.claim: Andy Summers says the Police adopted reggae bass lines because they suited Sting’s simultaneous playing and singing.

sources.title: Guitar Player: Andy Summers on the strategies behind his creative life
sources.evidence: Summers explains that spacious reggae bass lines enabled Sting to sing over his playing.

sources.title: LOS40: Interview with Andy Summers, 20 May 2022
sources.evidence: Separate interview: Summers describes Sting singing while playing reggae bass; distinguishes practical fit from a sweeping claim about Jamaican influence.

entries.claim: Nirvana closed MTV Unplugged with “Where Did You Sleep Last Night”, drawing on Lead Belly’s version of the traditional song.

sources.title: David Browne: In the Room at Nirvana’s MTV Unplugged in New York (Rolling Stone)
sources.evidence: Eyewitness account identifies the Lead Belly song as the final performance.

sources.title: Mike Powell: Nirvana — MTV Unplugged in New York (Pitchfork)
sources.evidence: Independent review identifies the Leadbelly cover, the In the Pines title, and its position at the end of the set.

entries.claim: Iron Maiden recorded a cover of Led Zeppelin’s “Communication Breakdown”.

sources.title: Metal Injection: Iron Maiden’s cover of Led Zeppelin’s Communication Breakdown
sources.evidence: Editorial account identifies the Zeppelin cover and its 1990 B-side release.

sources.title: Iron Maiden / Rhino-Parlophone: Communication Breakdown — official recording credits
sources.evidence: Official artist-channel recording, read via curl when browser fetch failed: credits Maiden as performer and Jimmy Page, John Paul Jones and John Bonham as writers; 1990 phonogram.

entries.claim: The Libertines recorded their debut album, Up the Bracket, with the Clash’s Mick Jones.

sources.title: Radio X: The Libertines on Up the Bracket, Mick Jones and Glastonbury
sources.evidence: Carl Barât interview recalls Jones producing the debut and introducing him to Clash music.

sources.title: The Independent: Carl Barât on the story of Up the Bracket
sources.evidence: Interview standfirst identifies the debut recording with Mick Jones.
